key_insight: Using statistically grounded, hard random benchmarks reveals that many prior claims of GNN superiority on constraint satisfaction problems are overstated — classical heuristics still outperform GNNs on truly hard instances. A fair, controlled benchmark is essential to evaluate solver performance.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standard, truly hard benchmark instances for evaluating Graph Neural Networks on constraint satisfaction problems, and the resulting risk of unsound comparisons with classical heuristics.
method: Construct hard random CSP benchmarks informed by statistical physics (phase-transition/hardness regimes).
Release the benchmark suite and evaluate multiple classical heuristics and GNN-based solvers on the same instance sets.
Perform fair comparisons under controlled budgets and metrics to measure solution quality and scaling on genuinely hard instances.
impact: Provides practitioners with a standardized, principled benchmark suite and reproducible evaluation protocol, encouraging stronger baselines, more realistic claims, and progress toward hybrid or improved ML+classical solvers.
visual_elements: Phase diagram indicating easy vs. hard regimes (parameter sweep from statistical physics).
Bar/violin charts comparing solver performance (solution quality, runtime) across hardness bins.
Pipeline flowchart: instance generation → solver set (classical vs GNN) → controlled budgets → metrics.
Iconic side-by-side comparison: classical heuristic vs GNN with runtime and success-rate badges.
paper_title: Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks in Solving Hard Constraint Satisfaction Problems
paper_authors: Geri Skenderi, Lorenzo Buffoni, Francesco D'Amico, David Machado, Raffaele Marino
